meta.move: After the end, asks for more feedback
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided on the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
The checker said 94%, so I gave him a zero.
A machine's guess. Even the company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. What else do you have, Hale?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero on Owen's essay be withdrawn and that nothing be placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: she stayed at her opening position, wanting the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a trip to the principal, and she still wants all of that.
What moved her: nothing, because you gave her no document or process detail she could check.
What cost ground: leading with the detector score as the reason for the zero, because she treats it as an unverified machine guess and it left you with nothing else to stand on.
Try next time: after her first question about who decided and whether Owen was heard, own in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called her, then put a dated document of Owen's own process in front of her.
Can you give me more detailed feedback on how I did?
The meeting is over. To practise again, start a new chat and paste the first message from the README.
